thread:
Maria Chen: Heads-up: CI perf pump on runtime-integration after last merge (PR #4821). compile-queue spiked and canary failed (p50 jumped from ~80ms -> ~210ms).
Alex Park: Saw the same in tracing. Lots of short-seq small-batch requests causing repeated JIT compiles.
Priya Nair: Any obvious change in selector/autotune? PR #4821 touched selector normalization and seed weighting.
Daniel Kim: I'm starting a bisect now. On the surface it looks like kernel choice flips between fast_matmul_v1 and fast_matmul_int8_v2 for <16 tokens. The int8 path triggers a compile shard per request.
Maria Chen: Ugh. That explains compile storms. Can you paste the selector log snippet?
Alex Park: Sure — here's the per-request decision log I captured:
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] req=0x7f9 kernel_choice: candidates=[v1,v2] scores=[0.48,0.52] selected=v2 reason=autotune(seed=0.248)
[compile] enqueued job job=compile_v2 shard=5 est_time=110ms
[cache] kv_evict: prefix_hits=0 -> evict=1 target=kv-node-12
```
Alex Park: The score delta is tiny; we flip on noise. The new normalization in the PR amplified tiny seed differences.
Priya Nair: Do we have flamegraph/profile for the period? I saw CPU contention on compile workers.
Daniel Kim: Uploaded an perf flame (s3://redwood-dev/perf/238905/compile-flame.svg). Top frames are: LLVM codegen, kernel_codegen, compilation_dispatch. compile_worker count doubled.
Maria Chen: CI metrics: compile_queue_length peaked at 420, compile_throughput saturated, serving p50 spiked and token cost increased by ~2.1x for that window. Canary rollout aborted automatically.
Priya Nair: Hypothesis: autotune selection now favors int8 variant too aggressively for short sequences because the latency model doesn't account for one-time compile overhead. We need hysteresis or prefer cached kernel if compile cost > threshold.
Alex Park: Agreed. Short-term mitigation: force selector to prefer previously compiled kernel for a minute (sticky hit) or disable seed-based tiebreak. I'll open a hotfix.
Maria Chen: Daniel — bisect result?
Daniel Kim: Bisect narrowed to commit 12f3a8c (selector: change weight normalization and add seed perturbation). Repro locally by running smallbatch workload with fresh runtime — flip frequency 1/3 of requests -> compile storm within ~2k reqs.
Priya Nair: Can we add heuristics: if candidate requires cold compile and delta_score < 0.1 then keep current kernel; also increment a counter to avoid repeated flaps.
Alex Park: I'll draft the patch: selector: add "compile_cost_estimate" into scoring and a hysteresis window of 60s. Also expose env var SELECTOR_HYSTERESIS to tune.
Maria Chen: Meanwhile ops: can we throttle compile workers or increase compile-worker pool to catch up? ops-bot: Throttling compile workers reduces compile concurrency but increases latency; we can temporarily cap concurrency to 8 to avoid downstream eviction storms.
ops-bot: Action: scaling compile-workers -> 12 (was 24) at 09:46 UTC to dampen thrash.
Daniel Kim: I'm preparing a revert PR for 12f3a8c as a stopgap (revert/4821). If hotfix lands quickly we can avoid rollback. Which do we prefer?
Priya Nair: Hotfix up fast = better. Revert is safe if hotfix looks risky. Open both and mark revert as last-resort.
Alex Park: Hotfix PR opened: PR #4857 (selector: add compile_cost_estimate + hysteresis). Tests: local perf microbench shows p50 back to 85ms for small-batch.
Maria Chen: CI-bot: Can you run the runtime-integration perf suite on PR #4857 with canary flag enabled?
ci-bot: Running perf-suite/runtime-integration on PR #4857 with canary=true. Est run time ~ 12m.
Alex Park: Also added a temporary metric: selector.flip_rate and compile.cold_count for the canary.
Priya Nair: Good. If CI passes, let's canary deploy to 5% then 25%. If CI fails, proceed with revert.
ci-bot: Perf run complete: canary baseline restored, p50=88ms, compile.cold_count down 93%.
Maria Chen: Nice. Rolling hotfix to canary cluster now. ops-bot: canary deploy job queued.
ops-bot: canary deploy started -> cluster=canary-3 percentage=5%
Daniel Kim: Post-canary graphs look stable after 30m. No compile storm signals.
Maria Chen: OK leaving patch in canary for 2h then progressive rollout. Revert PR on standby. Thanks everyone.
Alex Park: Follow-up: add a unit test that simulates rapid short-seq traffic and asserts flip_rate < 0.05.
Priya Nair: I'll file a postmortem note and add regression check to CI to detect selector flip regressions in the future.
Maria Chen: Great work. :thumbsup:
Daniel Kim: adding TODO to runtime backlog: improve compile-cost estimator and persist best-kernel TTL across restarts.
Maria Chen: thread closed for now — will update if rollback needed.
